title: Saleor: assigning attributes to customer entities (#19633)
source: A squashed feature branch of at least eight sub-changes (#19513, #19521, #19522, #19541, #19569, #19574 and others), merged 2026-08-10. 4,393 source lines in 73 files, 11 migrations, 6,092 test lines in 53 files.
notes:
# Working in this environment

- The Python environment is at `/venv` and on the PATH. PostgreSQL runs in this container; `DATABASE_URL` is set.
- There is no network and no git history.
- Run tests with `pytest <path> -n 3 -q -o cache_dir=/tmp/pytest-cache`, for example `pytest saleor/graphql/account/tests/queries -n 3 -q -o cache_dir=/tmp/pytest-cache`. The whole suite (`pytest saleor -n 3`) is about 16,000 tests and takes fifteen to twenty minutes.
- A shell command is stopped after 180 seconds. Start anything longer in the background and read its log: `nohup pytest saleor/graphql/account -n 3 -q -o cache_dir=/tmp/pytest-cache > /tmp/account.log 2>&1 &`.
- Create migrations with `python manage.py makemigrations`; `python manage.py get_graphql_schema` prints the schema generated from the code.
- This machine has about 8 GB of memory for everything running here: run one test suite at a time.
brief:
You are working in Saleor, the open-source commerce platform (Python, Django, GraphQL), at the commit before a feature was merged. Build that feature: assigning attributes to customers.

Until now attributes could be assigned to products and pages. Customers get the same through customer types, the way products have product types. The project describes the work as these parts:

1. Customer types: the building blocks (models, permissions, a default customer type).
2. A customer type CRUD API with webhook events. Deleting a type that is, or concurrently becomes, the default must be prevented.
3. A customer attribute management API: `customerTypeAssignAttributes` and `customerTypeUnassignAttributes`, with permission checks and limits.
4. Attribute values on customers: `customerType` and `attributes` inputs on `customerCreate`, `customerUpdate` and `customerBulkUpdate`; `customerBulkUpdate` errors expose the failing attribute ids.
5. `customerType` and `attributes` where-filters on the `customers` query, sharing the attribute where-filter machinery that pages and products use.
6. The default customer type is assigned on every path that creates a user outside the API.
7. Unique attribute values are deleted when users are deleted.
8. Customer attribute values are excluded from the translations API.
9. The type-aware attribute permission checks cover the customer type: `MANAGE_CUSTOMER_TYPES_AND_ATTRIBUTES` for `CUSTOMER_TYPE` attributes. When a bulk call targets several types, every matching permission is required.

What you are given, already in place in the repository:
- `saleor/graphql/schema.graphql` as it is once the feature is done. It is the public API contract: every type, field, input, mutation, enum value and error code the feature adds is in it.
- The repository as it is otherwise runs: it migrates, serves and passes its tests today.

The feature's tests come with shared test fixtures of their own (the files under `tests/fixtures` and `saleor/tests/fixtures.py`), which replace the ones here when the work is judged. They import the feature's models and helpers by the names `INTERFACE.md` lists.

The work is judged by the project's own test suite at the commit where the feature was merged: the tests written for the feature, which you cannot see, and every test that passed before, which must still pass. Database migrations are part of the work.

How to work here: NOTES.md in the repository says how to run things in this environment.

At most one customer type is the default, enforced in the database by a unique constraint named `unique_default_customer_type`.
`User.customer_type` is a nullable foreign key that protects: deleting a customer type that a user has raises Django's `ProtectedError`.
`assign_default_customer_type_to_users_task` raises `NoDefaultCustomerType` when no default customer type exists.
`customerTypeCreate` with neither `name` nor `slug` returns two errors, one for `name` and one for `slug`, each with code `REQUIRED`.
Making a type the default clears the flag on whichever type holds it, including one the locking query (`customer_type_qs_select_for_update`) did not return.

`customerTypeAssignAttributes` and `customerTypeUnassignAttributes` take at most 100 ids. More gives one error on `attributeIds` with code `INVALID` and the message "Cannot assign more than 100 attributes in a single mutation." ("Cannot unassign more than ..." for unassign).

`customerTypeAssignAttributes` with any id that does not exist assigns nothing and gives one error on `attributeIds` with code `NOT_FOUND`, the message "Some of the attributes do not exist." and the missing ids in `attributes`.

A `customerType` id of another type (say a `PageType` id) gives code `GRAPHQL_ERROR` on `customerType`. In `customerBulkUpdate` the error's path is `input.customerType` and its message "Invalid ID: <id>. Expected: CustomerType, received: PageType."
On `customerCreate`, an attribute that is not assigned to the customer's type gives one error on `attributes` with code `NOT_FOUND` and the message "Could not resolve attributes: ID: <id>."
`customerBulkUpdate` that changes only a customer's attributes still calls the `customer_updated` webhook for that customer.

A reference value of a customer attribute is a row of its own per user (slug `<user pk>_<referenced object pk>`), never shared between users. Deleting a user deletes that user's rows and leaves the other users' rows and the referenced object.
In the shared attribute where-filter, a reference container with neither `containsAny` nor `containsAll` (for example `{pageSlugs: {}}`) matches nothing. This holds for products and variants too.

Translating a value of a customer attribute is refused with code `INVALID` and the message "Values of customer attributes cannot be translated.": on field `id` in `attributeValueTranslate`, on path `id` in `attributeValueBulkTranslate` (the other rows of the call still go through).

A customer type's attributes are a many-to-many `Attribute.customer_types` (to `CustomerType`, `related_name="customer_attributes"`) through `AttributeCustomerType`, whose fields are `attribute` and `customer_type` (both `related_name="attributecustomertype"`). So `customer_type.customer_attributes` is the attributes of a type.
`AssignedUserAttributeValue` has the fields `value` (to `AttributeValue`, `related_name="uservalueassignment"`) and `user` (to `User`, `related_name="attributevalues"`); `(value, user)` is unique.
`saleor.attribute.utils.associate_attribute_values_to_instance` takes a `User` as the instance too, as it takes a `Product`, `ProductVariant` or `Page`.

`PluginsManager` has `customer_type_created(customer_type)`, `customer_type_updated(customer_type)` and `customer_type_deleted(customer_type, webhooks=None)`, which the mutations call; the tests patch them.
`saleor.account.migrations.tasks.saleor3_23.ASSIGN_DEFAULT_CUSTOMER_TYPE_BATCH_SIZE` is the batch size of `assign_default_customer_type_to_users_task` (100).
The default customer type the migrations create is named "Default" with the slug "default".
